title: Freddy Hardest
uncounted: loaded with the game, after floor_four_course_pairs ($2352)
loaded with the game, after title_colours_lower ($265C)
loaded with the game, after base_panel_colours_bottom ($3518)
loaded with the game, after choose_movement_frames ($8441)
loaded with the game, after f_9DCA ($9DCA)
loaded with the game, after draw_base_panel ($B507)

records.c: Sets bitmap display and uses named KERNAL loads to fetch separate resources. Stops in a self-jump at $0B54 after the last load.
Adjacent load names used by the bitmap loader, starting with C.B, C.A and PIC.
Installs the title raster handler and copies title assets. Loops through the access-code form until $1137 is set, then waits for a fire input or key redefinition.
Stores the five default matrix indexes into $3BBD through $3BC1.
Updates the five title control text rows and waits for keyboard samples through the helpers at $0D61 and $0D77.
Uses $1134 and $1135 to time the title animation, setting sprite zero's pointer, X coordinate, X high bit, colour and visibility.
Clears the title sprite and background state, selects the VIC bank and text page and initializes the colour and position of sprite zero.
Copies 140 cells each from $24B8 and $2544 and their colours from $25D0 and $265C. Appends the five small title text rows.
Clears four pages of screen cells at $4400 and initializes the corresponding four colour pages at $D800, then clears colour entries at $D800 through $D8FE.
Stops CIA1 timer A, installs the VIC raster handler at $1055 and schedules its first interrupt at line zero.
Banks out KERNAL, then copies five runs from the RAM under it beginning at $F800 to the title character area starting at $5398.
Copies five overlapping runs starting at $FC30 into the upper panel character cells at $5398. The source pointer wraps through $FFFF during the last run.
When the input position is zero, copies the prompt cells from $115A and enables digit collection at position one.
When the next digit position is 6, compares entered glyphs at $1141-$1145 with $113B-$113F. A match sets $1137 and clears the screen. A mismatch resets the entry position.

Scans the keyboard through $CAF8 and uses the ten indexes at $1146 to look up a numeric key. Writes its glyph to the screen and to $1140 plus the digit position, waits for release, then increments that position.
Acknowledges VIC interrupts. On a raster interrupt, signals the title loop and selects VIC bank $4000, custom glyphs at $5000 and screen matrix $4400.
Twenty-four cells for the program credit written to the first text row beneath the title.
Twenty-four glyphs for the graphics credit.
Twenty-four glyphs for the title copyright line.
Twenty-four glyphs for the key configuration legend.
Twenty-four glyphs for the prompt to start the base.
Five expected digits in the private font's character codes. They read 25425.
Ten indexes into the keyboard scan result at $2904. The parallel bytes at $1150 hold the glyph code for each key.
Glyph numbers $64 through $6D for the digit keys in the order 0 through 9.
The twelve private-font cells for ACCESS CODE, including the two blanks between the words.
Floor 1 map stream. Each pair indexes the upper and lower eight-cell columns in the dictionary at $2AF8.
Later column pairs from the same floor stream, up to the bound selected at $BC61.
Floor 2 map stream beginning at $1A52. The dictionary is at $2DE8.
Final map pairs before the floor-2 bound selected at $BCCA.
Floor 3 map stream beginning at $1F52. It reuses the dictionary at $2AF8.
Map pair stream selected by the fourth floor setup. Its column dictionary starts at $30A8.
First 140 character cells copied by $0E9A to build the title art.
Second 140 character cells for the title art.
Colour cells matching the first 140 title character cells.
Colour cells matching the second 140 title character cells.
Eight-tile vertical column records at the dictionary base shared by floors 1 and 3.
Eight-tile vertical column records used when floor 2 is active.
Eight-tile vertical column records used by the fourth floor.
Upper panel tile source at $3338. The copy mirrors it to both screen pages.
Lower panel tile source at $33D8, mirrored the same way.
Upper panel colours copied to colour RAM starting at $DAA8.
Lower panel colours copied to colour RAM starting at $DB48.
Character shapes used when D018 selects $5000. The small letters and digits at $4C-$71 are used on the access-code screen and title.
Upper half of the $5000 glyph set. The tile codes $80 and higher include pieces of the title lettering and its surrounding artwork.
VIC sprite shapes in 64-byte slots, starting with Freddy's upper and lower body frames. Each image uses the first 63 bytes of its slot.
Further 64-byte sprite slots containing alternate facing and posture frames and the small isolated action shapes interleaved with them.
Player animation slots at pointer numbers $80-$88. Body parts are stored as separate hardware sprite images.
VIC sprite shapes in 64-byte slots, including further character poses and shapes for the base inhabitants and their animation.
Sprite slots from pointer $99, including split body poses used by the moving character groups.
Sprite slots from pointer $A9, containing more character poses followed by small point and burst shapes.
Sprite slots from pointer $B9, containing burst and flash shapes as well as the first of the next group's body poses.
Sprite slots from pointer $C9, including small images and the upright and leaning poses in the latter half of the block.
Sprite slots from pointer $D9, containing body parts for a sequence of character poses.
Sprite slots from pointer $E9, including the final poses and their mirrored or shifted counterparts shown in the sprite sheet.
Last six populated sprite slots starting at pointer $F9, containing left- and right-facing standing poses.
Banks out BASIC and calls the cartridge header restoration at $81C7 before continuing into the title and game initializer.
Clears the display and initializes the base state, then calls $0BB8 for the access-code and title screens before setting up the first floor.
Seeds action, panel and terminal flags on entry to base play, including $3AF5, $3B06 and $3AB3 with 2.
Copies five header bytes from $92AC to $8004 and writes the cold and warm start vector bytes at $8000-$8003.
Selects the $4000 VIC bank via CIA2 and initializes scroll, screen selection and base display flags.
Updates the panel and player state, calls the movement dispatcher and selects the joystick or keyboard input routine using $3BB7.
Dispatches on input in X. When the active-low mask is $09, sets $3AF5 and $3BB5 to 1 before continuing through the movement logic.
Indexes one of the tables at $9219 and $9221 using $3B06 to write both player shape pointers, then calls the cell check for that path.
Tests $3B7D and updates player sprite pointers, colour, action fields and the byte at $926D.
Tests the active action $3B0B and updates the action flags at $3C02-$3C04 as well as $3B7D and $3B92.
Tests bit 4 of $3ACC before updating the sprite group position and state at $3A30 through $3A38.
Forms coordinate limits beginning with $3A30 and tests them against the other positions and flags involved in first-row contact.
Builds working bounds starting from the position at $3A3E, tests against $3A42 and selects an update for the second row or the neighbouring first-row group.
Changes first-row sprite pointers and position values after counting eight at $3B82.
Changes second-row sprite pointers and position values after counting eight at $3BE5.
Requires player Y reference $44 for the first path and examines the collision state at $3B0C. Updates the sprite group's position bytes and sound pointer where applicable.
Uses the same kind of collision input for the $84 player row, updating the opposing group's position bytes at $3A3A and $3A3B.
Tests the active bit in $3B80 and updates the paired coordinates at $3A30 and $3A32 and their sprite flags.
Tests the active bit in $3B84 and updates the paired coordinates at $3A3E and $3A40.
Dispatches on $3BE7. States 3 and 4 both jump to $8A82. Other paths can adjust sprite pointers $3A24 and $3A25.
Dispatches on $3BE8. States 3 and 4 both jump to $8B6B. Other paths can adjust sprite pointers $3A3A and $3A3B and the group flags.
Checks Freddy's $44 row reference and examines the group flag at $3A38. Some contact paths request a new sound and mark the group's phase at $3BE7.
Tests player Y reference $3B91 for $84 before processing the sprite group whose coordinate and condition bytes include $3A42, $3BE5 and $3BE8.
Tests request flags $3BD0 and $3BD8 and sets sound stream pointer $3BEB-$3BEC and its state before calling the driver.
Calls $AA1E twice. The first generated byte determines the flag at $3B7E through a comparison with $96. The next is compared with $55 and $AF to choose a state at $3B7D.
Initializes $3B8C-$3B8D and writes corresponding panel cells in both screen buffers, with player-sprite state changes on subsequent paths.
Tests bit 7 of $3B80, then selects a first-row frame using $3BE6 and the table at $9DB0.
Tests bit 7 at $3B80 before moving the group at $3A30. Some paths change the sprite frame state at $3A24 and call $951E.
Selects new sprite frame values according to the action at $3B7F and updates the paired coordinates and enable shadow.
Uses $3B83 to dispatch animation updates and changes the group positions and flags at $3A47, $3A48, $3ACC and $3BB4.
Handles state $3C00 and copies matching indicator glyphs to cells in both screen pages.
Skips the update when $3C00 is 5. Otherwise updates position and frame bytes and can change sprite 2's colour.
Tests the saved sprite collision mask at $3B0C for bit 2 before changing the sprite position and state.
Updates the leftgoing cell index, then checks bit 2 of the saved sprite overlap before updating position and action flags.
Increments the active sprite's cell index and searches both screen matrices for the relevant blocking tile in the selected row.
Decrements the cell index and tests the opposite-direction tile in both screen matrices.
Takes a seven-glyph row from $9E26 through the offset table at $9E49 and mirrors it at $42E0 and $46E0. The two-byte count at $3BBA advances the word selection.
Dispatches on the movement result at $3B9E. Some paths check lift position tables or call the ship-position lookup at $A119.
Steps the flags at $3BCC and uses the icon index at $3BCD to select a sprite pointer and colour during the terminal interaction.
Searches four low and high byte pairs at $ACAB and $ACAF for the current map cursor. A match saves the index and sets the transition flags.
Compares the coarse map cursor at $3A68-$3A69 with four ship position pairs at $ACB3 and $ACB7. On a match records the index at $ACA6 and sets the transition flags.
Copies four seven-glyph rows from $AD55 plus the selected row index times seven. The indices at $AD35-$AD38 select the text copied into $AD39-$AD54.
Advances $3BCB and updates character cells on both screen pages every third count while the terminal display is active.
Fills four rows of panel cells on both screen pages and initializes the ship selection and message paths.
Dispatches on $3BCA. Stages 1 and 2 check the selected ship's readiness bytes, then queue the matching hyperspace or energy-cell status text for $A94B.
Clears four message bands on the active $4000 or $4400 screen selected by $3B8E.
Calculates a destination on the active $4000 or $4400 screen from row $3BD4 and column $3BD5, then resets the displayed-character count for the message.
Every third count in $3BD7, advances the message copied to the screen through $FD and updates the message cursor and ready flags.
Copies its two-byte input state at $3B2A-$3B2B to the working bytes at $3B2C-$3B2D, then applies the shift and add update.
Shifts the working two-byte value left Y times, then adds the starting state.
Initializes 12 bytes from $ACC4 to $FF and writes the colour-code state used by the terminal logic.
Fills tables at $ACAB, $ACAF, $ACB3, $ACB7 and $AE06. Branches on bit 7 of $3B2D and uses the result of calls to $AA1E.
Tests bit 1 of the base UI flags at $3BCC, then updates the panel cells at $42E9, $42EA, $4311 and $4312 and their counterparts on the second page.
Copies entries from the paired map position tables to $ACA7-$ACAA, then updates the old table slots.
Writes the temporary position bytes at $ACA7-$ACAA back into the corresponding table entries.
Seven-glyph rows used by $A462 to assemble short terminal messages, including the words for nuclear cell and ship.
Screen glyph data for hyperspace and energy-cell readiness, the captain code and ship choice prompt, and the launch and ending messages.
Clears the three voice request bytes and zeroes the 25-byte SID shadow at $3A49.
Copies the 25-byte shadow at $3A49 to the SID at $D400-$D418.
Selects voice 1 and consumes the request and stream state at $3BF7, $3BEB-$3BEC and $3BEE-$3BEF.
Selects voice 2 and consumes the corresponding request state at $3BF8 and stream pointer at $3BF0-$3BF1.
Selects voice 3 and consumes the corresponding request state at $3BF9 and stream pointer at $3BF2-$3BF3.
Loads the saved voice-1 stream pointer into $65 and selects register shadow $3A49 through $67.
Selects the voice-2 stream pointer and its shadow starting at $3A50.
Selects the voice-3 stream pointer and its shadow starting at $3A57.
Initializes and copies part of a voice event through the pointers at $65 and $67 and updates the event position at $3BED.
Interprets the flags at $B42C and calls sound-parameter handlers. Updates the event cursors in $3BED and $3BFA.
Reads successive parameter bytes through the pointer at $65, using $3BED as the stream offset, and stores voice state beginning at $3A5E.
Reads parameters from the stream pointer at $65 and prepares the first timer state at $B42E-$B431.
Reads parameters from the same stream and prepares the second timer state at $B432-$B435.
Reads the next byte into offset 3 of the voice shadow and sets further state at $B436-$B438.
Decrements the timer at $B42F and updates the selected parameter through $67 when the timer expires.
Decrements $B433 and returns if the event has time remaining. On expiry reloads it from $B434 and writes voice state through the indexed table and pointer at $67.
Clears four pages at $0400 before building a room.

Copies the two panel tile bands to both screen matrices and their colours to colour RAM. Starts with index $A0 and includes index zero, so each transfer writes one extra position beyond its 160-cell band.
Copies cells from offsets 1 through 39 of each row to the cell on their left, repeating for X rows and stepping the screen pointer by 40.
Uses a four-phase row-group index to choose source and target addresses from the page pointer tables before calling the row-copy loop.
Uses the active page and the current row-group index to prepare pointer arguments for the opposite scroll direction.
Copies selected source row cells backwards to the destination row one cell farther right, preserving the source order when the pages coincide.
Copies the source row starting at column one to the destination starting at column zero, and updates the row pointers for the next of X rows.
Chooses the next or previous map pair according to $3AB0, then draws the corresponding edge of the active screen page.
Reads a pair of column IDs through the map cursor at $3A68, advances it by two bytes and passes the IDs to $B749.
Resolves the entering column pair when scrolling backwards, using the course cursor and the column addressing helper.
Adds eight times each ID in $3A81 and $3A82 to the selected floor dictionary pointer. Returns the two addresses through $FB and $FD.
Writes tile bytes through $FB and $FD to column 39 of the first screen page, starting at $4027 and $4167 for the two groups of rows.
Writes the two groups of new tile bytes to column 39 of the second screen page, starting at $4427 and $4567.
Writes tile bytes through the two source pointers into column zero of the first screen page, beginning at $4000 and $4140.
Writes the incoming left-edge tiles into the second screen page at $4400 and $4540 and subsequent rows.
Draws forty columns into scratch RAM at $0400. For each column it writes eight character codes in both strips separated by $140 bytes, using a stride of 40.
Sets the scrolling counters at $3B19-$3B1F and initializes source and destination pointers used to prepare the display.
Initializes $FB to point to the scratch screen at $0400 and sets up screen destination pointers at $F7 and $F9 for the two live matrices.
Banks out the KERNAL and copies eight pages from the source at $FB into the live glyph RAM at $4800, then restores the ROM and reenables interrupts.
Fills each 40-cell colour RAM row with the byte from $CA62 indexed by X. Starts at $3BA8 and stops when X reaches $3BA9.
Compares the cursor to the active floor lower bound and adds the configured span when the low byte is below its threshold.
On its end-of-course test, subtracts the span from the map cursor and restores the appropriate high-byte base.
Looks up a course position in the pairs at $CA22 and $CA32. On a match sets the lift sprite position and enable bits, and remembers the result index.
Compares the fine scroll position in $3AF2-$3AF3 against the pairs at $CA42 and $CA52. On a match writes sprite position and enable state and stores the index at $3ACA.
Uses the active page flag to prepare screen pointers at $C8 and $CA and writes through them.
Dispatches on the floor number at $3B18. Selects a glyph source for $BA70 and sets row colour bounds, comparison glyphs and sprite-related parameters for that floor.
Loads glyph source $E000 and sets the dictionary at $2AF8 and stream bounds $1352 and $1942.
Loads glyph source $E800, dictionary $2DE8 and map bounds $1A52 and $1E6E.
Reuses the $E000 glyphs and the $2AF8 dictionary while selecting the map bounds $1F52 and $2224.
Loads glyph source $F000 and selects the $30A8 dictionary and map bounds $2352 and $2438.
Selects the first screen matrix in the VIC bank and resets page and transition variables. Initializes the paired Y-position mirrors at $3A29 and $3A2B at a spacing of $15.
Uses state $3B07 to select a transition, updating $3AD9 and the player sprite coordinates or pointers along the branches.
Uses phase $3AA5 to pick a raster line from $C98B. Clears the high raster compare bit and leaves the display enabled.
Tests neighbouring cells in the active page against the floor-specific character values. Can revise sprite pointers, sound requests and the player action.
Tests the relevant cells in the active tile matrix against the per-floor values at $3B97-$3B99. Some exits set $3B9E. A match at $C22C can set both player sprite frame pointers and schedule action 3.
Checks X for $0C before advancing action state at $3B09 and updating the two player sprite frame pointers.

When $3AF5 is 1, subtracts four from the first sprite Y shadow and stores it in both shadows. Subtracts $2B from the first sprite pointer, sets the second pointer to the next value and sets $3AF5 to 2.
Per-row colour table. Floor setup puts the starting and ending offsets in $3BA8 and $3BA9.
Clears the 65-byte sample at $2904 and rotates an active-low column select through CIA1 port A. Tests port B bits and maps five configured key indexes to an active-low control mask in $3BB8.
Reads CIA1 port A and leaves its five low bits in $3BB8. Fire is active low at bit 4.
Stops CIA1 timer A, sets raster compare $8D and enables raster interrupts, then installs $CBD0 in the KERNAL IRQ vector.
Acknowledges VIC interrupt status and selects the processing phase from $3AA5. Two of its phase entries are $CCB0 and $CC83.
Inserts the scroll bits indexed by $3A99 into the low field of D016.
Decrements the two-byte course position at $3AF2-$3AF3 and writes the horizontal fine-scroll field from the table at $CFA3.
Increments the two-byte course position, stopping at the floor-specific bound in $3BA5-$3BA6, and updates D016 from the fine-scroll table.
Increments first-group X values and adjusts their per-sprite high bits and enables.
Increments second-group X values and updates their high bits and enables.
Decrements the X bytes of the first moving sprite group in pairs and adjusts their flags.
Decrements the X bytes of the second moving sprite group and adjusts $3A42 and the group flags.
Sends the first sprite group's coordinates to VIC registers and synchronizes the frame pointers on both screen pages.
Sends the second-row sprite group's positions, frame pointers, colours and masks to the VIC and both screen pointer tables.
Scroll bits selected by $CD28, $CD6D and $CDBF before writing D016.
Pairs of bit masks used by the sprite coordinate and enable helpers.
Glyph bytes stored beneath the KERNAL. Floor selection 1 passes this address to $BA70 to copy 2048 bytes to $4800.
High-index half of the $E000 floor character set. The copy to $4800 places these glyphs at $4C00-$4FFF.
Source for the second-floor character bank. Floor case 2 at $BC76 passes $E800 to $BA70.
High-index half of the second-floor set. These bytes replace the same live glyph addresses at $4C00-$4FFF.
Source of the floor glyphs selected by the default case at $BD48 in the floor setup.
High-index half of the $F000 character set, copied for the default floor to $4C00-$4FFF.
Source for the character patch copied to $5398 by $0F40 before drawing the entry screen.
Tail of the first source band. The second source starts at $FC30, within the last run of the first.
Character patch selected by $0F8E when leaving the title. It replaces the corresponding title glyphs in live memory.
